mechanism_narrative: A higher level of real GDP (GDPC1) indicates a stronger economy, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is consistent across economic cycles, with the GDP level serving as a leading indicator of equity market performance.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 and 20-day S&P 500 returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate falls below 0.5%, it signals an active monetary easing policy that reduces discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% occurs in more than 40% of the time, but 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) indicates a weak economic recovery with limited monetary policy flexibility, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 8.0%, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 8.0%) is associated with economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 8.0%, 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 95.0, it signals robust manufacturing activity and strong economic growth, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 95.0 occurs in more than 40% of the time, but 60-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: High housing starts (HOUST > 500) and strong retail sales (RSAFS > 380000) indicate robust consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 500 and RSAFS > 380000, 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity and economic growth, which is associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The relationship is consistent across economic cycles.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 20-day S&P 500 returns is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 220.0, it signals elevated inflation expectations that may lead to monetary tightening and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 220.0, 5-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
